clue.text: High point when Carmen's screened regularly, duck

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Carmen's screened, starting with the first

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: An opera fan watching Carmen on a screen, punctuated by an instruction to duck.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of CARMENSSCREENED give CRESCEND, and duck, a zero score in cricket, supplies the final O.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is loosely used for a climax or peak, the moment of greatest intensity.

clue.text: Incentive that could cause an MOT failure?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reward offered to encourage someone, as opposed to the stick

definitions.text: that could cause an MOT failure
definitions.meaning: second meaning: split three and three, ..., the rust that fails a vehicle's MOT, the annual British roadworthiness test

explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly safety test for British cars; corrosion can fail it.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a reward dangled to motivate, from the donkey led on by a vegetable.

clue.text: English trees are rubbish!

parts.note: the yew and the ash are two trees, so the one word supplies both names in turn

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on English trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense or claptrap, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Cooking Cornish fare near historic county

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are prepared afresh in a new mix

explanation.surface: Preparing Cornish food somewhere near an old county.
explanation.definitionFit: Caernarfonshire was a Welsh county abolished in 1974, now part of Gwynedd.

clue.text: Woman or man cycling

indicators.note: cycling says the end letter of or man goes round to the front

explanation.surface: A man or woman out on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: ORMAN with its final N moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a female forename, so it can stand for a woman in crosswords.

clue.text: Depose and gain this extra run

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to remove a ruler from power
second meaning: in cricket, a run scored when a fielder's throw evades the stumps and goes on

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is cricket: an extra run from a wild throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To overthrow a ruler is to topple him, and in cricket a misfield's overthrow yields bonus runs.

clue.text: Boy Scouts left holding nothing round

indicators.note: round says the assembled letters are turned about and read backwards
holding says the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Scouts on the left of a camp sit holding nothing as they gather round.
explanation.walkthrough: PORT holding O gives POORT, which turned round reads as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouts are organised into units called troops, so a body of Boy Scouts is a troop.

clue.text: This is serious … my fish supper costs less!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for a moment of crisis
second meaning: read literally, the price of chips has fallen

explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips is a British takeaway meal, so a cheaper supper has chips that are down.
explanation.definitionFit: When the chips are down is an idiom for a critical, testing situation.

clue.text: End is not in reach

parts.note: not in means out
to reach a place is to come to it

explanation.surface: A note that the finish line is out of reach.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcome is the result or conclusion of a process.

clue.text: Bolshie salesperson possibly coming up with lines

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is one kind of salesperson
verse consists of lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A stroppy sales rep arriving with a prepared script.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolshie is British slang for awkward or uncooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: Perverse means contrary and stubbornly unreasonable, much like bolshie.

clue.text: Animal came 'ither by boat, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says we want words that sound like the phrase spoken

parts.note: to come hither by boat is to have rowed here; with the dropped aitch of the clue, rowed 'ere

explanation.surface: A dialect speaker reporting that someone came here by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'rowed 'ere' matches the two-word answer; the apostrophe in 'ither drops the H just as 'ere does.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small European deer species, so it is a kind of animal.

clue.text: Regular terminus — no less — for Badminton Horse Trials participant

parts.note: regular, as in smooth or uniform, means even

indicators.note: no here says the word that follows is to be removed from terminus

parts.note: taken as written
less in arithmetic is minus

explanation.surface: A sporting note about a horse competitor at the end of the line, with an odd aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking MINUS (less) out of TERMINUS leaves TER. Badminton Horse Trials is a famous English three-day equestrian event, not the racquet sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a rider or horse competing in three-day eventing, the discipline contested at Badminton.

clue.text: Welsh prince of old, on the wagon

parts.note: wain is an archaic word for a farm wagon or cart

explanation.surface: A medieval Welsh prince who has given up drink, being on the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the wagon' looks like a phrase meaning teetotal, but the wagon is just a wain.
explanation.definitionFit: Owain Glyndŵr led a Welsh revolt around 1400 and was proclaimed Prince of Wales.

clue.text: Cut of meat from China to be cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared in a new arrangement, like food worked over in the kitchen

explanation.surface: A recipe note about a joint coming from China that is to be cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The aitchbone is the rump bone of cattle, and the beef cut taken over it bears the same name.

clue.text: Tedious job — go back and review sharper routine planners

parts.note: a chore is a tedious job

indicators.note: back says the word go is to be read in the opposite direction
review means looking over the letters again and recasting them

explanation.surface: A dull task: go back and check some sharper routines.
explanation.walkthrough: CHORE, then GO turned back as OG, then RAPHERS from sharper rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Choreographers devise dance routines, planning the sequence of steps performers follow.

clue.text: Perhaps Yoko doesn't fancy being alone

parts.note: Yoko Ono is the artist who married John Lennon

indicators.note: fancy says the letters of doesn't are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: Yoko Ono doesn't like being on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: Fancy looks like a verb meaning like, but it is the anagram signal. On one's tod is British slang from rhyming slang (Tod Sloan, own).
explanation.definitionFit: On one's tod is British slang for by oneself, solitary.

clue.text: Crusades' wheels? They're old, but not that old!

definitions.text: They're old, but not that old

indicators.note: wheels as a verb means turns about, so the letters are spun round

explanation.surface: The vehicles of the medieval crusaders, joked about as old but not ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: Wheels looks like a noun for cars, but it signals the anagram; the crusades were a series of medieval expeditions, hence old.
explanation.definitionFit: Used cars are second-hand vehicles: previously owned, yet not antiques.

clue.text: Pod and house sea loch flows wildly around

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the house abbreviation
wildly says the letters of sea loch flows are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A Scottish scene of water flowing wildly around a house by a sea loch.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea loch is a Scottish inlet of the sea; 'Pod' looks like a pea pod but is a group of marine mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is a group of whales or dolphins swimming together, the same idea as a school.

clue.text: One who doesn't believe in roast chicken

parts.note: to roast is to heat
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A sceptic who doesn't trust roast chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen is someone outside a religion, regarded as an unbeliever or pagan.

clue.text: Self-opinionated chap, number one out of 10, received top place

indicators.note: number one out of says take just the first letter of what clue 10 supplies

parts.note: a cross-reference to the answer of clue 10 across, eventer
received means got
1st, first place, written as IST

explanation.surface: A conceited man ranks himself first out of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 points to the answer of 10 across, whose first letter is E; 1ST written with I for the numeral one gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: An egotist is a person excessively absorbed in himself and his own importance.

clue.text: Havoc when firing ship's missiles

indicators.note: firing is read as fire into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
havoc, total mayhem, can be called hell

explanation.surface: Chaos aboard as a warship fires its weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Shells are explosive projectiles fired from guns, a form of missile.

clue.text: Approaches swan swimming in bleak surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings says the bleak word goes around the rearranged swan

parts.note: drear is a poetic word for bleak or dismal

indicators.note: swimming suggests the swan's letters moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: A swan drifts closer across a cold, dreary lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Drear is a literary, rather old-fashioned form of dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw near is to come closer, the same as to approach.

clue.text: Field of interest in some future almanac

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A specialist subject covered in a forthcoming almanac.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a domain or sphere, as in the realm of science.

clue.text: Sandy's exclamation after record time

indicators.note: after says the exclamation is placed following the record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
och is a Scots exclamation; Sandy is a stock Scottish name

explanation.surface: A Scot named Sandy cries out after setting a record time.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandy, short for Alexander, stands for a typical Scotsman, whose exclamation is OCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long era or period in history, a span of time.

clue.text: One who doesn't believe where robber is working?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who denies the existence of God
second meaning: read as two words, at a heist, the place where a robber is busy

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer two and five to see the robber's whereabouts.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist is a non-believer, rejecting any deity or religious faith.

clue.text: Unfriendly US spies invading Laos on manoeuvres

indicators.note: invading says the spies go inside the other letters
on manoeuvres says the letters of Laos are moved about

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: American agents carrying out a hostile incursion into Laos during military exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On manoeuvres' fits the military surface, but here it signals the anagram of the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial describes someone avoiding company or interaction with others, so not sociable or friendly.

clue.text: Japanese martial arts instructor's endless opinion

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a sensei is a teacher of a Japanese martial art

explanation.surface: A judo teacher who never stops giving his views.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after instructor is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense can mean a view or judgement, as in the sense of the meeting.

clue.text: Is in total charge around Maidstone

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of Maidstone are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone running everything in and around Maidstone, a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to control or rule over, so dominates is holding complete command.
